headline: Cyber Resilience Act duties loom; Hamburg funds digital twin pilots

summary.text: CRA vulnerability reporting duties already apply from September 2026, with full obligations in December 2027, so makers of connected products need security processes now.
A joint position on Cyber Resilience Act and Machinery Regulation challenges points to overlapping obligations that machine builders must plan for together.
A sensor maker's practical CRA case (Kübler, Sendix S58) shows how security documentation and vulnerability reporting can be combined with safety work.
Hamburg's new grant instrument for digital twin projects could co-finance a mid-sized plant's twin pilot.
MVTec, BMG and Bosch Rexroth are simplifying machine vision integration on ctrlX, and CBAM now allows crediting third-country carbon prices, which could lower costs for steel and aluminium importers.

actions.text: Product and quality leads should check whether your connected products have a vulnerability-reporting process in place, since CRA reporting duties already apply, and start a gap analysis against the 2027 obligations.
Machine builders should have TMG consultants map overlaps between CRA and Machinery Regulation obligations in one joint compliance plan, rather than running two separate projects.
Plants in Hamburg considering a digital twin should check eligibility and application deadlines for the new grant. Plants adding AI inspection on ctrlX should look at the MVTec/Bosch Rexroth offer.
